title: Welcoming a Neighbor for Coffee
description: Set out cups and a small tray before a neighbor arrives.
cardDescription: Set out cups and a small tray before a neighbor arrives.
focus: The setting is welcoming a Neighbor for Coffee. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Drink made from roasted ground beans
Small dish placed beneath a teacup
Movable panel at a room's entrance
Tap on a door to announce a visit
Tip liquid from one container into another
Flat serving container with a raised edge
Happy expression with an upturned mouth

answerNotes.COFFEE: Coffee is brewed from roasted beans. The familiar beans are actually seeds from the coffee plant's fruit.
answerNotes.CUP: Cup can name a drinking vessel or a measuring amount. A recipe's measured cup is not simply any small mug.
answerNotes.SUGAR: Sugar sweetens baking mixtures and drinks. Granulated sugar and powdered sugar have different textures despite sharing the same sweet ingredient.
answerNotes.CREAM: Cream is the rich part of milk. Whipping adds air, which is why whipped cream becomes fluffy.
answerNotes.CHAIR: A chair is intended for one sitter. A bench or sofa generally provides room for more than one person.
answerNotes.DOOR: A door is the movable panel at an entrance. Hinges let it swing, while a latch or lock holds it closed.

answerNotes.FAMILY: Family can include several generations and relatives by marriage. A family tree shows relationships rather than everyone's physical appearance.
answerNotes.PHOTO: Photo is short for photograph. A caption or name label can preserve information that the image alone does not supply.
answerNotes.TABLE: A table provides a raised flat surface. Chairs are the separate furniture used to sit beside it.
answerNotes.NAME: A name identifies a person or thing. In a family album, adding names helps later readers recognize the people pictured.

answerNotes.PRICE: Price is the amount asked for an item. Change is money returned after a customer pays more than that amount.
answerNotes.TABLE: A table provides a raised flat surface. Chairs are the separate furniture used to sit beside it.
answerNotes.COIN: A coin is a metal piece of money. The value depends on the currency and period; Bible stories do not use modern U.S. coins.
answerNotes.CHANGE: Change is the money returned when payment exceeds the price. The word can include several coins rather than just one.
answerNotes.BOOK: A book has pages joined inside a cover. The title names the work; the author is the person who wrote it.
answerNotes.LAMP: A lamp provides light from a fuel or electrical source. Bible lamps used oil rather than a modern bulb.
answerNotes.CHAIR: A chair is intended for one sitter. A bench or sofa generally provides room for more than one person.
answerNotes.TOY: A toy is made for play. A miniature model can be a toy, a hobby project, or a display depending on its use.
answerNotes.SIGN: Sign can be a public notice or the action of writing a name. Check whether the clue describes an object or asks for a verb.
answerNotes.BOX: A box is a container rather than its contents. In a hobby clue, a kit may come in a box but the two words are not interchangeable.

subtheme: A Welcome Basket for New Neighbors
description: Give new neighbors a small collection of practical gifts and local information.
cardDescription: Give new neighbors a small collection of practical gifts and local information.
focus: The setting is a Welcome Basket for New Neighbors. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Greeting offered to a new neighbor
Piece of stiff paper carrying a message
Food baked from flour and dough
Sweet produce such as an apple
Someone whose home is close to yours
Panel opened to enter a room

answerNotes.BASKET: A basket is made by weaving flexible material. Its open structure and carrying handle make it useful for collecting garden produce.
answerNotes.CARD: Card can mean a printed greeting or a playing piece. An envelope points to a greeting; a deck or suit points to a game.
answerNotes.NOTE: A note is a short written message. It can be a reminder, a greeting, or a brief explanation attached to an object.
answerNotes.BREAD: Bread may be a whole loaf or pieces cut from it. A loaf is counted as a whole, while a slice is one flat portion.
answerNotes.FRUIT: Everyday fruit dishes can mix several kinds of plant produce. The serving word is culinary and does not require a botanical classification.
answerNotes.SOAP: Soap helps remove dirt when used with water. Rinsing carries away the loosened dirt and remaining suds.
answerNotes.TOWEL: Towels absorb water after washing or swimming. Their looped fabric holds more moisture than a smooth hard surface.
answerNotes.RIBBON: A ribbon is a narrow fabric strip. A looped bow and a straight trailing tail are different parts of a tied ribbon decoration.
answerNotes.DOOR: A door is the movable panel at an entrance. Hinges let it swing, while a latch or lock holds it closed.
answerNotes.GIFT: A gift is something given, rather than sold. A tag identifies the recipient; wrapping protects or decorates the present.
